# Reading

All reading is from the course textbook, [Illowsky and Dean, *Introductory Statistics 2e* (OpenStax)](https://openstax.org/details/books/introductory-statistics-2e).
A copy of the PDF is also available: [Introductory Statistics 2e (PDF)](../assets/introductory-statistics-2e_-_WEB.pdf). Page numbers are the
printed page numbers of the book; in the PDF, add 12 to find the page.

## Week 1
*Introduction; describing and visualizing distributions*

Chapter 1: Sections 1.1 - 1.3, p. 5 - 33

## Week 2
*Distributions and frequency tables; shape; dot plots, stem-and-leaf plots and histograms; measures of location*

Chapter 2: Sections 2.1 - 2.3, p. 66 - 93

Chapter 2: Sections 2.5 - 2.6, p. 98 - 106

## Week 3
*Measures of spread, boxplots, cumulative distributions*

Chapter 2: Section 2.4, p. 94 - 97

Chapter 2: Sections 2.7 - 2.8, p. 107 - 119

(Cumulative relative frequency is in Section 1.3, p. 26 - 33.)

## Weeks 4 - 5
*Sampling designs, sampling and nonsampling error, experimental design, research ethics*

Chapter 1: Section 1.2, p. 10 - 25

Chapter 1: Sections 1.4 - 1.6, p. 34 - 42

## Week 6
*The normal distribution, z-scores and outliers; sampling distributions and margin of error; introduction to probability and random variables*

Chapter 6: Sections 6.1 - 6.2, p. 335 - 346

Chapter 7: Section 7.1, p. 365 - 369 (the sampling distribution of the mean and its standard error)

Chapter 3: Sections 3.1 - 3.5, p. 167 - 195

Chapter 4: Sections 4.1 - 4.2, p. 227 - 236

## Week 7
*Discrete and continuous probability distributions*

Chapter 4: Section 4.3 (binomial), p. 237 - 241, and Section 4.6 (Poisson), p. 250 - 254

Chapter 5: Section 5.1, p. 291 - 294

## Week 8
*Sampling distributions and the central limit theorem; introduction to confidence intervals*

Chapter 7: Sections 7.1 - 7.3, p. 365 - 380

Chapter 8: Section 8.1, p. 405 - 415

## Week 9
*Confidence intervals for a proportion and for a mean; choosing a sample size*

Chapter 8: Sections 8.1 - 8.3, p. 405 - 426

## Week 10
*Significance tests and P-values; tests for a proportion and for a mean*

Chapter 9: Sections 9.1 - 9.6, p. 461 - 485

## Week 11
*Composite hypotheses; confidence intervals and tests; types of error and power; introduction to two-sample tests; comparing two independent proportions*

Chapter 9: Section 9.2 (Type I and Type II errors), p. 464 - 465

Chapter 10: Introduction, p. 511; Section 10.3 (Comparing Two Independent Population Proportions), p. 523 - 527

The sign test is not in the textbook; see the lecture notes for that week.

## Week 12
*Comparing two independent proportions or means; matched pairs (dependent samples); introduction to categorical data; goodness-of-fit tests and tests of independence*

Chapter 10: Sections 10.1 - 10.5, p. 512 - 535

Chapter 11: Sections 11.1 - 11.5, p. 563 - 583

## Week 13
*Cramer's V, McNemar's test, Fisher's exact test; measures of association*

These topics are not in the textbook; see the lecture notes for that week.

## Week 15
*Correlation and simple linear regression; the coefficient of determination, tests for the slope, checking assumptions*

Chapter 12: Sections 12.1 - 12.6, p. 617 - 643

## Week 16
*Analysis of variance (ANOVA): comparing several means; multiple comparisons*

Chapter 13 (one-way ANOVA), Sections 13.1 - 13.3, p. 679 - 689. Multiple comparisons are not in the
textbook; see the lecture notes for that week.

# Extra Problems

***These problems are not required, but they are recommended for practice.*** Answers to the
odd-numbered problems are in the Solutions section at the end of each chapter.
